newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan construction shares rise on recovery hopes.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan construction shares rise on recovery hopes.

text.p: Shares in Taiwan's construction sector rose by mid-morning on Wednesday on hopes that a long-awaited recovery in the domestic property market might occur in the second half of 1997, brokers said.
With 75 minutes left, construction stocks had risen 1.55 percent, while the overall index was down 0.34 percent.
Pao Shiang was up 50 cents, or 1.32 percent, to T$38.5 and Chang Ku Building rose 50 cents, or 1.77 percent, to T$28.8. Both shares were among the 10 most heavily traded shares.

"Investors now believe the expected property market recovery will arrive in the second half of this year because many investors have gained money from recent stock market rallies, and they tend to use the money to buy houses that can more secure the value," said HSBC James Capel analyst Alex Chen.
The January industrial output figures announced on Tuesday also brought a welcome sign of new life for the market.

Though real estate and construction industry output fell an annual 12.21 percent in January, land area for which construction firms have sought development permits rose 17.37 percent, the economics ministry said.
It was the second straight month of double-digit growth for the land-under-permit indicator.
